## Internship Admission Requirements

Candidates coming to the University of Massachusetts Global Internship program from another University must end their current internship credential with their previous university and complete the restriction change.

To be admitted to an Internship Program at University of Massachusetts Global, an applicant must:

1. Be admitted into a University of Massachusetts Global stand alone or MAT credential program for Multiple Subjects, Single Subjects, Education Specialist;
2. Meet with an Education Clinical Coordinator to obtain information about these internship credential options and eligibility;
3. Provide verification of subject matter competency (Multiple Subject, Single Subject Credential or Education Specialist programs);
4. Provide proof of meeting U.S. Constitution requirements;
5. Provide a copy of a negative T.B. clearance or TB Risk Assessment;
6. Provide an active Copy of a Certificate of Clearance or any active permit issued by the CTC to teach P-12 in a public school;
7. Complete program specific 120-hour pre-service requirements for Internship Credentials. Please meet with your Education Clinical Coordinator for pre-service course requirements;
8. Complete the Intern Eligibility Application which is found in the Credential Support Hub;
9. Submit a completed Verification of Employment (VOE) form to an Education Clinical Coordinator. The VOE form must be approved by the Education Clinical Coordinator. Once the VOE is approved, the student can be placed in class and will receive an email directing them to pay for their internship credential on CTC online. Payment must be received by CTC within 90 business days.

## Requirements to Maintain Internship Credential

Internship candidates must maintain a 3.0 GPA and be continuously enrolled in Clinical Practice courses. Candidates must maintain a log of hours documenting support/mentoring and supervision.

An intern who does not enroll in courses for two or more consecutive sessions may be ineligible for the intern credential.

If a student’s employment is terminated by the district or the student, the student must contact the Education Clinical Coordinator immediately.

## California Teaching Performance Assessment (CalTPA)

The state mandated California Teaching Performance Assessment is required for Multiple and Single Subject, and Education Specialist candidates. The assessment consists of two instructional cycles based on the pedagogical sequence of plan, teach and assess, reflect and apply. Each of these four steps is addressed by each instructional cycle. Candidates complete cycles during Clinical Practice. Cycles are submitted through Pearson and candidates pay a fee to submit each cycle. Candidates who fail either of the two cycles must retake the cycle and pay the associated fee. Both cycles must be passed to be recommended for the Multiple Subject, Single Subject, or Education Specialist Credential. Candidates that have a clear credential or have already passed a Teacher Performance Assessment may be exempt from the CalTPA and should consult with their advisor.

## Recommendation for Credential

Upon successfully completing and passing all credential, program and coursework requirements, the candidate may apply to be recommended to the CTC for the credential. For single subject candidates, the content specific methodology course must align with the subject matter competency route. To apply for the credential, candidates complete the Recommendation Form in the Credential Support Hub. Once the recommendation is made by the Office of Credentials and Clinical Practice (OCCP), candidates complete a CTC exit survey and submit the credential fee.

# University of Massachusetts Global.

Detection status
    Turnitin's AI writing detection is confirmed in current use for faculty. The Center for Instructional Innovation's own faculty-training page is headed "Plagiarism and AI Detection Tutorials For Brightspace," includes a tutorial on "Enabling and Managing TurnItIn Settings on Assignments in Brightspace," and separately curates "Additional Resources on Turnitin's Artificial Intelligence (AI) Writing Detection" for instructors. No university statement on the evidentiary weight of an AI-detection result was located.

Office in these sources
    Office of Academic Support · (800) 746-0082 · academicsupport@umassglobal.edu

Ombuds or advocacy office
    Office of Student Concerns (OSC) — "an advocate for the fair resolution of a problem, not for any particular party," giving "equal attention to the rights for all concerned." Institutional contacts: Justyn Howard, Director of Student Conduct and Ombudsman Services/Title IX Coordinator, and Alex Pappas, Student Affairs Specialist · ombuds@umassglobal.edu · umassglobal.edu — Complaint Policy

Reproduced from the institution's own pages quoted below — potentially relevant official sources, not a determination of which one governs any case.

UMass Global's published sources on AI detection and academic integrity, quoted and linked below. UMass Global is a private nonprofit university within the University of Massachusetts System but operates its own, separate Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity — it is not governed by the policies of UMass Amherst, Boston, Lowell, or Dartmouth. These are potentially relevant official sources, not a determination of which one governs any case — course syllabi and program-specific documents may also apply. Confirm applicability with the institution. Any dates are quoted from the sources, not a deadline calculation performed for you.

01Detection status

## Turnitin's AI writing detection is confirmed for faculty use, alongside its similarity checker

The Center for Instructional Innovation's faculty resource page on academic integrity (part of UMass Global's own instructional-support site; retrieved Oct 25, 2026) is headed:

"Plagiarism and AI Detection Tutorials For Brightspace:"

Under that heading, it links faculty training on "Enabling and Managing TurnItIn Settings on Assignments in Brightspace" and "How to Check Assignments and Discussions for Similarity." A separate section of the same page, headed "Using TurnItIn To Detect Plagiarism," states: "Turnitin solutions promote academic integrity, streamline grading and feedback, deter plagiarism, and improve student outcomes," and points instructors to tutorials on "Turnitin Plagiarism Detection and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Checker tools." The page then curates a further section:

"Additional Resources on Turnitin's Artificial Intelligence (AI) Writing Detection"

linking directly to Turnitin's own AI-writing-detection FAQ, its explanation of the capability's false-positive rate, and its guidance for instructors on "Approaching a student regarding potential AI misuse." Source: Center for Instructional Innovation — Academic Integrity (Faculty). The linked Turnitin materials are the vendor's own content, curated here as a faculty resource; they are not quoted as UMass Global's own statement, and no UMass Global-authored sentence on the evidentiary weight of an AI-detection result was located on this page or in the Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity (quoted in full below).

The Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity itself (in the public 2026-2027 Academic Catalog; retrieved Oct 25, 2026) governs AI use directly without naming a detection tool:

"Submitting work completed using any AI tool without instructor permission is prohibited. When faculty require the use of technology, including artificial intelligence, as a part of an assignment for the course, there is no violation. Students are reminded to consult syllabi, assignment sheets/rubrics, program documents and their faculty. Use of artificial intelligence, when permitted, must be correctly cited in the assignment."

Source: Undergraduate Credit-Hour and MyPath Academic Policies and Procedures. The library's own Artificial Intelligence Resource Guide for Faculty (retrieved Oct 25, 2026), which links to the same CII page, offers a process-based alternative to relying on a detector score:

"Engaging in a conversation with the student and exploring their understanding of the paper's content is an important step in addressing any concerns."

Source: Academic Integrity and GAI — Artificial Intelligence Resource Guide for Faculty.

Named-vendor sweep (Turnitin and its AI-writing indicator specifically, SimCheck, Originality, Copyleaks, iThenticate, GPTZero, Originality.ai, Winston AI, Crossplag, ZeroGPT, Packback, Grammarly Authorship, Honorlock, Proctorio, Respondus, Examity) against umassglobal.edu, its library guides, and its instructional-support site found Turnitin confirmed as above, including its AI-writing detection capability specifically; no other listed tool is named anywhere. Active or former attorneys may not be present in a GAC panel hearing, as the process is not meant to be a hearing of law." Recording of the hearing is not addressed anywhere in the policy. — Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity, Section D (Governance and Appeals (GAC) Hearing) · Undergraduate Credit-Hour and MyPath Academic Policies and Procedures

What follows on the record
    "A formal dismissal for a violation of academic integrity will be recorded on the student's official transcript. Students dismissed due to an academic integrity violation are not eligible for readmission to the University." No transcript, retention, or disclosure provision is stated for a lesser sanction. — Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity, Section C.8 (Investigating and Reporting) · Undergraduate Credit-Hour and MyPath Academic Policies and Procedures

The two questions an adviser raises first, answered from this institution's own published documents — or recorded as not stated in them.

UMass Global's Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity (2026-2027 Academic Catalog; retrieved Oct 25, 2026) places the first determination with the instructor: faculty "investigating the incident(s), determining through evidence, subject matter expertise, and professional experience whether or not a violation of this policy has occurred." No evidentiary standard — such as a preponderance of the evidence — is named anywhere in the policy for either the Dean's review or the GAC hearing; this is a genuine absence, stated rather than assumed. The GAC panel instead decides "based on whether or not a violation(s) actually occurred, evidence and appropriate information provided during the Dean's review and/or during the GAC hearing, university policies, and procedures."

"If the student does not agree with the sanctions imposed by the instructor... the student may work with an advisor to submit a petition within 10 business days of being informed of the imposed sanction." "[T]he student may request a hearing with the Governance and Appeals Committee (GAC), within 10 business days of receiving the Dean's decision." "A student has the right to appeal within 30 business days of notification by the GAC of the academic integrity decision... The appeal decision will be rendered by the Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor of Academic Affairs. The appeal decision will be final and binding."

Source: Undergraduate Credit-Hour and MyPath Academic Policies and Procedures. What these quotations mean for any particular case is for the institution and its process to determine; they are reproduced so you can read the originals in context.

### Why Accreditation Matters

Regional accreditation is the baseline requirement: it determines eligibility for federal financial aid and is what most employers and other colleges check first when evaluating whether a degree, or its transfer credits, will count. AACSB accreditation is a more specialized signal specific to business programs, reflecting curriculum rigor and faculty credentials that matter most for employer recognition in competitive hiring and for those who may later pursue a deferred MBA program. AACSB is not required for financial aid eligibility, but it can strengthen a resume in ways a regionally accredited program alone may not.

### Total Cost Ranges

Factoring tuition, fees, and program length together, a full 120-credit online BTM degree generally costs between $38,000 and more than $58,000 in 2026. Accelerated 60-credit completion tracks for students with substantial transfer credit typically range from $15,000 to $35,000, a meaningful discount for those who qualify.

> (08-22-2025, 09:48 AM)redheadguy03 Wrote: I got my application in. My advisor person never responds to my emails though. So is it just a waiting game on the application?

Congrats on applying, and yes, it is a waiting game! The process is like many other MBA programs. Apply, attach transcripts if you have them, and send official transcripts. There are a few internal stops it goes through: academic verification and requirements approval; pilot program approval; and new student ID number, student school e-mail and welcome email set up. Since the original target date of September 2nd is fast approaching you might be approved sooner than later, but I would give it until next Thursday.  I was able to keep things flowing by emailing [email protected] when I sent my official transcripts, and then I alerted them when I could see in my Parchment account that UMG had downloaded them. I did have a very responsive Enrollment Coach, but also I made sure to take time to make a connection with her, and establish a rapport. On our initial conversation I asked if she could email me periodic updates and help to oversee things from her view.  I do believe her interactions and follow-up in the process made a difference.
